nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. Every production $A \to \alpha'$ of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating $\varepsilon$-productions arises from a production $A \to \alpha$ of $g$ with the same left-hand side $A$, such that $\alpha'$ is obtained from $\alpha$ by deleting some occurrences of nullable nonterminals and $\alpha'$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: Productions of the $\varepsilon$-eliminated grammar come from productions of $g$

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. For every production $A \to \beta$ of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions, there are a nonterminal $B$ and a production $B \to \beta$ of $g$ such that $\beta$ is not a single nonterminal and $B$ is reachable from $A$ by a possibly empty chain of unit productions of $g$.
nodes.title: Productions of the unit-eliminated grammar come from non-unit productions of $g$

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ and every word $w$ over its terminals, $w$ is generated by the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating $\varepsilon$-productions if and only if $w$ is generated by $g$ and $w$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: The $\varepsilon$-eliminated grammar generates the nonempty words of $g$

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$, no production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating $\varepsilon$-productions has empty right-hand side.
nodes.title: The $\varepsilon$-eliminated grammar has no empty productions

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$, the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating $\varepsilon$-productions has the same nonterminals and the same initial nonterminal as $g$. Its productions are the productions $A \to \alpha'$ such that $g$ has a production $A \to \alpha$, the form $\alpha'$ is obtained from $\alpha$ by deleting some (possibly no) occurrences of nullable nonterminals (those deriving the empty word in…
nodes.title: Elimination of $\varepsilon$-productions

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $V$ an assignment of a language $V(A)$ to each nonterminal $A$ of $g$ such that the empty word belongs to $V(A)$ whenever $A$ is nullable (derives the empty word in $g$). If a sentential form $\alpha'$ is obtained from a sentential form $u$ by deleting some occurrences of nullable nonterminals, then the language denoted by $\alpha'$ under $V$ is contained in the language…
nodes.title: Deleting nullable nonterminals shrinks the denoted language

nodes.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$ over an alphabet $T$ there is a context-free grammar $g'$ over $T$ that generates exactly the nonempty words generated by $g$, such that no production of $g'$ has empty right-hand side and no production of $g'$ has a single nonterminal as its right-hand side.
nodes.title: Existence of reduced grammars

nodes.summary: For a sentential form $u$, a finite word of terminal and nonterminal symbols, the nonterminals of $u$ form the finite set of all nonterminals that occur in $u$.
nodes.title: Nonterminals of a sentential form

nodes.summary: The nonterminals mentioned by a context-free grammar $g$ form the finite set consisting of the initial nonterminal of $g$, the left-hand side of every production of $g$, and every nonterminal occurring in the right-hand side of a production of $g$.
nodes.title: Set of nonterminals mentioned by a grammar

nodes.summary: A context-free grammar is reduced when no production has empty right-hand side and no production has a single nonterminal as its right-hand side.
nodes.title: Reduced grammars

nodes.summary: A sentential form is a unit output when it consists of a single nonterminal.
nodes.title: Unit output

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and, for each nonterminal $A$, let $L_g(A)$ be the language of words $g$ derives from $A$. Then $L_g$ is a valuation of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating ε-productions: for every production $A \to \alpha$ of that grammar, the language of $\alpha$ under $L_g$ (the concatenation of the languages of its symbols, a terminal $a$ denoting $\{a\}$) is contained in $L_g(A)$.
nodes.title: Soundness of ε-production elimination

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and, for each nonterminal $A$, let $L_g(A)$ be the language of words $g$ derives from $A$. Then $L_g$ is a valuation of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions: for every production $A \to \alpha$ of that grammar, the language of $\alpha$ under $L_g$ (the concatenation of the languages of its symbols, a terminal $a$ denoting $\{a\}$) is contained in $L_g(A)$.
nodes.title: Soundness of unit-production elimination

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and, for each nonterminal $A$, let $L_g(A)$ be the language of words $g$ derives from $A$. If $B$ is reachable from $A$ by a chain of zero or more unit productions $A \to A_1 \to \dots \to B$ of $g$, then $L_g(B) \subseteq L_g(A)$.
nodes.title: Languages along unit chains

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar with a production $A \to u$, and let $\alpha$ be a nonempty form obtained from $u$ by deleting some (possibly no) occurrences of nullable nonterminals. Then $A \to \alpha$ is a production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating ε-productions.
nodes.title: Productions of the ε-free grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and let $B$ be reachable from $A$ by a chain of zero or more unit productions of $g$. If $B$ is the left-hand side of some production of $g$, then $A$ is among the nonterminals mentioned by $g$ (its initial nonterminal, the left-hand sides of its productions, and the nonterminals in their right-hand sides).
nodes.title: Unit chains start at mentioned nonterminals

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, let $B$ be reachable from $A$ by a chain of zero or more unit productions of $g$, and let $B \to \beta$ be a production of $g$ whose right-hand side $\beta$ is not a single nonterminal. If $A$ is among the nonterminals mentioned by $g$, then $A \to \beta$ is a production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions.
nodes.title: Productions of the unit-free grammar

nodes.summary: In a context-free grammar in which no production has an empty right-hand side, every nonempty sentential form yields only nonempty words.
nodes.title: No empty words without empty productions

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ and a sentential form $u$, the nullable deletions of $u$ are the forms obtained from $u$ by deleting any selection of occurrences of nullable nonterminals, possibly none and possibly all, keeping the remaining symbols in order. They form a finite set.
nodes.title: Nullable deletions

nodes.summary: A nonterminal $A$ of a context-free grammar $g$ is nullable when $g$ derives the empty word from $A$.
nodes.title: Nullable nonterminal

nodes.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$, the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions generates the same language as $g$.
nodes.title: Eliminating unit productions preserves the language

nodes.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$, no production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions has an output consisting of a single nonterminal.
nodes.title: Eliminating unit productions leaves no unit production

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. For every production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions, some production of $g$ has the same output.
nodes.title: Eliminating unit productions creates no new outputs

nodes.summary: A unit production is one whose output is a single nonterminal. For a context-free grammar $g$, the grammar obtained by eliminating unit productions has the same nonterminals and the same start symbol as $g$. Its productions are the $A \to \alpha$ such that $A$ is a nonterminal mentioned by $g$ (its start symbol or one occurring in a production of $g$), $g$ has a production $B \to \alpha$ that is not a unit…
nodes.title: Eliminating unit productions

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. A nonterminal $A$ of $g$ reaches a nonterminal $B$ by unit productions when there is a chain $A = A_0, A_1, \dots, A_n = B$ with $n \ge 0$ such that each $A_{i-1} \to A_i$ is a production of $g$. In particular, every nonterminal reaches itself.
nodes.title: Reachability by unit productions

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ of $g$ yields a terminal word $w$ in $g$, then some form $\alpha'$ obtained from $\alpha$ by deleting some occurrences of nullable nonterminals yields $w$ in the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating $\varepsilon$-productions, and $w$ is empty if $\alpha'$ is empty.
nodes.title: Completeness of eliminating empty productions

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ of $g$ yields a terminal word $w$ in $g$, then $\alpha$ yields $w$ in the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions.
nodes.title: Eliminating unit productions keeps every yield

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
